name: J. A. Marshall's dancing school

proprietors.name: J. A. Marshall
proprietors.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card marshall_j_a (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

staffing.principal_is: J. A. Marshall, this record's proprietor, who advertises the tuition, sets the hours and sells the tickets himself.

hands.basis: period_convention, off the staffing model's `school` class, whose own row reads `schoolteacher` — the same office under the business layer's word for it: an assistant at the larger schools only, and the model's typical is 0 because the town's schools of 1835 are one room and one teacher. Its analogue is the 1839 list's thirteen schoolteachers, four years and some three thousand people after the scene.
hands.why_not_drawn: No source reached names a second person teaching with Marshall. The dancing school hires a ROOM and not a staff: it met in Messrs. Johnson & Stevens' Assembly Room at the New York House, and the people of that house are the tavern's, not the school's.

attendance.basis: NO FIGURE IS PRINTED, AND THE NOTICE IS THE OPPOSITE OF A COUNT: 'Those wishing to become pu[p]ils will please leave their address at the Ex[c]hange Co[ff]ee House.' That is a school advertising for a class it does not yet have. It does divide the class it hopes for by hour — 'Miss[e]s and young Mas[t]ers, from 2 until 5 o'clock, P. M; and from 6 until 9 for the elder class of Gentlemen' — which is a shape and not a number.

staffing.basis: THE TEACHER OF A ONE-ROOM SCHOOL IS THE PERSON WHO KEEPS IT, and this record already names them. The staffing model gives the class one role, an assistant, at 0–0–1 with a typical of nought; drawing one here would put a second schoolteacher in a room the model says held one. So the answer to 'who taught here' is a pointer at a row this record carries, not a new row beside it.
staffing.replaceable_by: Any printing that names a second person teaching at this school — an assistant, an usher, a monitor — would draw the hand above. A roll, a quarterly return or a subscription list would give the attendance a figure for 1835 instead of a silence.

locations.basis: Placeable against the committed town. The landmark is the committed structure exchange_coffee_house.
locations.limit_reason: The register places this house against exchange_coffee_house and the town holds no roof of its own for it (action: new_building), so the anchor is as far as the reading goes.

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1834-11-19, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read british: J. A. Marshall (british). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A directory, a deed or a later reading that names this house's premises, its staff or its dates more exactly than the newspapers do.
